summary: First live exercise of myiotsan's Modbus WRITE path, against tools/sunspec-sim (tools/fleetbench/bench_iotsan_modbus.py). Commanding a polled device - a solar inverter, a battery - ends in modbus.WriteConfirm, which writes once, reads the register back, and never re-issues. That is the right design and it is also self-certifying: a write that went to the wrong register, the wrong unit, or with the wrong sign confirms itself exactly as happily as a correct one, because it reads back whatever it wrote wherever it wrote it. So the bench brings its own Modbus TCP client and reads the simulator directly, and because a register is not the point either - a curtailment that lands in the right register and changes nothing is a confirmed command that did nothing - every write is checked three ways: the app's status, the raw word on the wire, and what the plant does next, read back through the product's own telemetry. It found one, in the configuration path rather than the write path: a SunSpec profile that declares NO telemetry keys was polled happily and stored nothing at all, in complete silence. A SunSpec profile needs no register bindings because it discovers its datapoints, but a sample whose key the profile does not declare is dropped by design - so a profile with no keys reads the device perfectly and keeps none of it. The poller logged that it was polling every two seconds, the device's Last seen kept advancing (liveness is deliberately recorded before the keys are consulted), no error was raised anywhere, and the only trace was `decoded: 0` buried in GET /api/devices/stats. An integrator sees a connected inverter with an empty chart and nothing to explain it. The register-map mode has always refused the equivalent profile out loud; the SunSpec mode now refuses it too, naming what to fix, with a unit test guarding that no shipped SunSpec builtin ever trips the new refusal. Everything else about the write path held up and is now proven rather than assumed: a curtailment reaches the real holding register, reports confirmed, and the inverter really throttles (its operating state changes to THROTTLED and its AC power drops below the cap); the sign convention is right - a setpoint of -40 on an i16 register is 65496 on the wire, not clamped and not refused, and a 0.1-scaled -12.5 is 65411; every actuation gate holds on the Modbus transport and a refused command leaves the register untouched, which only a read of the wire can show; a write that cannot land (an unmapped register, an unreachable device) ends failed, says plainly it was not confirmed, and is recorded exactly once with nothing retrying it; and the same guarded path works for a NON-SunSpec device through a hand-authored register map, where the vendor inverter throttles to the written limit and recovers when it is lifted. 30/30 against the fix, 29/30 against unfixed main.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no API, schema or configuration change. One behaviour changes, and only for a profile that could never work: a SunSpec-mode Modbus profile that declares no telemetry keys is now refused by the poller and logged as not pollable, where before it was polled and silently stored nothing. No shipped builtin is affected (a unit test pins that), and any site profile with at least one declared key behaves exactly as before. The simulator, which is developer tooling and not shipped, gains a -tod flag to start at a chosen hour and an export-limit control register on its non-SunSpec unit so a write to that device is observable rather than merely stored.
